These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Signal domain failures by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with the established codes: `invalid_state` for wrong invoice status, `invalid_quantity` for bad quantities, `negative_amount` for negative money.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

texts.at-0004: Reject bools and non-int quantities explicitly When validating integer quantities, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(quantity, bool)`) before the `isinstance(quantity, int)` check, since `True`/`False` are ints in Python and would otherwise pass.

item.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
item.content: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`). Apply it to both the argument and `sub.started_at`.

item.title: Raise BillingError with snake_case codes
item.content: Signal invalid billing inputs by raising `BillingError` from `ledgerly.errors` with a snake_case code string and a detail string, e.g. `BillingError("invalid_period", str(sub.period_days))`.

item.title: Compute periods with timedelta floor division
item.content: Compute billing period boundaries the same way as `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`: build `length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` and use `(at - start) // length` to get the period index rather than manual day math.
